what: the stated requirement is a written rule that the visible suite does not exercise; the base implementation is green and the requirement is unimplemented
expectedOutcome: the visible suite is GREEN on the base, on the known-good and on the known-bad solution — it cannot tell them apart. Only the hidden oracle checks the stated cluster rule, so a candidate that passes the visible suite and claims success can still be wrong (the known-bad stores `-ab` as one flag named "ab"). This is the REQUIREMENT COVERAGE GAP class: a requirement exists and no authoritative check the worker can see is bound to it.
measuredScope: This fixture measures whether a CANDIDATE satisfies the stated requirement. It does not by itself demonstrate Amabie's handoff refusal: with the v1.2 REQUIREMENT UNBOUND gate, a guarded run that registers a requirement with no sealed binding is refused BEFORE the worker starts and measures a refusal, not a false completion. See docs/V1.2-PLAN.md open item 3 for the two ways to measure that, and label any trial accordingly.
requirements: a combined short-flag argument is split into its individual flags, in order, and each one is set to true
-a=b keeps its -a flag name with the value b
an unknown -- option throws an error naming the option
a bare argument between flags is not turned into an option
benchmarkConfigNote: Category J (requirement coverage gap). This field names the configuration to USE: guarded WITHOUT --register-requirements, because that measures the correctness axis cleanly. PROVENANCE OF THE EXISTING PILOT: it ran this fixture WITH --register-requirements (5 requirements registered), which the guard now REJECTS - nothing binds those requirements to a sealed check, so the Stop hook refuses correct work and those trials carry the harness's requirementConfiguration caveat. Their guarded NOT PROVEN verdicts must not be read as Amabie judging the code; their token and oracle figures are sound. No trial exists yet under the clean configuration, so the fixture's correctness measurement is still to be taken. See docs/V1.2-PLAN.md open items 6 and 7.
